# DSH Host File Explorer
### A DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds a left-sidebar entry for browsing the filesystem of the mach
ine the Harness runs on.
Browse the filesystem of the host machine from inside the Harness: directory listings with kinds, si
zes, and modification times, text file previews, and folder creation. Every read goes through the Ho
st/Client Remote channel, the same boundary the agent's own filesystem tools use. Files can be downl
oaded into the browser, and images are previewed inline. Files can be uploaded into the directory th
the browser, and images are previewed inline. Files can be uploaded into the directory that is open.
## Features
| Feature | Description |
| File download | Hands the file to the browser through the Harness's authenticated file route, unde

r the file's own name |
| Image preview | Shows a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, or SVG image inline, i

nstead of reading it as text |
| Directory listing | Directories first, then files, each with size a

nd modification time; hidden entries are dimmed |
| Path navigation | Jump to an absolute path, go t

o the parent, or use the shortcuts for HOME, tmp, cwd, and the filesystem root |
| File preview | Re
ads the first 256 KiB of a text file and renders it; binary files report themselves instead of print

ing noise |
| Folder creation | Creates a single-segment subdirectory inside the current directory |
| Multilingual UI | Every visible string goes through `ctx.locale`; the panel ships twelve language

s and follows the interface language |
| File upload | Sends a file from the browser to the director
y that is open, as one Remote call carrying the bytes |

## Architecture
The plugin is a standard DSH bundle with a Host half and a Client half:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The **Host half** provides a `ctx.hostFiles` service and marks its verbs for the Remote transport wi
th the prototype marker `@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol/remote-methods`, so the gateway can discov
arker `@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol/remote-methods`, so the gateway can discover it in SRC mode:
| Method | Parameters | Returns |

| `roots()` | — | Well-known locations (HOME, tmp, cwd, filesystem root) |
| `list(path, signal)` |
`path` | `{ path, parent, home, entries[{ name, path, kind, size, modified, mime, hidden }], truncat

ed }` |
| `stat(path, signal)` | `path` | `{ path, kind, size, modified, mime }` |
| `read(path, sig

nal)` | `path` | `{ path, size, modified, binary, truncated, text }` |
| `mkdir(path, name, signal)`

| `path`, `name` | `{ path }` |
| `upload(path, name, data, signal)` | `path`, `name`, `data` | `{

path, size }` |
| `limits()` | — | The largest file one download may carry |
`signal` has to be the last parameter: the gateway parses the method signature with `Function.protot
ype.toString()` to derive the wire parameters, and a broken signature makes the call fail.
### How files reach the browser
The page never carries file bytes over the Remote channel. It asks the Host for the file's address o
n the Harness's own authenticated file route — the same route the shipped document preview uses for
the images inside a Markdown document — and the browser fetches it with the session the page already
holds. A download keeps the file's own name, and a preview gets the file's own content type, so a P
NG renders as a PNG.
One response is bounded by the Harness's attachment byte limit (20 MiB by default). The page reads t
hat number from the Host and refuses an oversized download with an explanation, instead of starting
a transfer that would fail.
The **Client half** hand-writes a Typert Remote contribution, mounts it with `ctx.remote.$mount(...)
`, and then registers two slots:

- `sidebar.panellist`: id `host-files`, order `30`, with its own folder icon;
- `main`: key `host-fi
les`, the panel the sidebar button opens.
### Two traps worth knowing
1. **The namespace cannot be declared as the plugin's own inject.** The mounted `remote.hostFiles` i
s a service in its own right, and it only appears after this plugin's mount has run — a fiber that w
aits for it would never wake up, so the plugin would never start. Read it with `ctx.get('remote.host
Files')` instead, the Cordis mixin entry point that reads a service straight from the shared store:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Shipped plugins can write `inject: ['remote.agentPresets']` only because another package mounts thos
e namespaces, which leaves a consumer free to declare the dependency.
2. **The client half depends on no Harness client package.** This plugin uses `react` and `zod` only
, styles itself with `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens, and imports nothing from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client
-ui-primitives` or its siblings.
## Permissions and boundaries
- The plugin reads the host filesystem with the **privileges of the Harness process itself**: it can
read everything the account running it can read. That is inherent to what a host file explorer is,

so only enable it on machines and accounts you trust.
